description: The USAGE clause's per-item endianness-phrase and encoding-phrase (ISO §2023:13.18.60.2 general format: FLOAT-BINARY-32/-64/-128 [ endianness-phrase ], and FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/-34 with a bracketed choice-indicator group over { encoding-phrase, endianness-phrase }) — a COBOL-2014 addition arriving with the standard floating-point usages themselves. §2023:13.18.60.4 GR19a/b give the phrase its meaning (HIGH-ORDER-LEFT = big-endian, HIGH-ORDER-RIGHT = little-endian) and GR19c/d make the OPTIONS FLOAT-BINARY / FLOAT-DECIMAL clause supply the IMPLIED phrase only where the item states none — so the item's own phrase WINS, per §2023:11.9.8.3 SR2/SR3's 'in which an endianness-phrase is not specified'. Recognition-based on the parsed floatFormatPhrase, like the noSignPhrase row above: the phrase is a modifier, not a usage keyword, so it cannot be keyed on the resolved Usage enum. Annex A.3 item 18 makes the phrase processor-dependent AND requires that when the FLOAT-BINARY clause is supported, the USAGE-clause phrases match it — WiseOwl COBOL supports both phrases in both places.
vcr: 2014 introduction (§2023:13.18.60.2 endianness-phrase / encoding-phrase on the USAGE clause; arrives with the standard floating-point usages)

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. UFFP.
